prompt-engineering.description: Underspecified prompts are about twice as likely to regress across model or prompt changes.[1]

context-engineering.description: Anthropic treats context as a finite resource with diminishing returns and aims for the minimal set of information that fully outlines the expected behavior, which is not necessarily short. In coding-agent studies, repository overviews did not help; that non-standard specifics help is plausible and reported by one source, not established.[1][2]

harness-engineering.description: Anthropic's remedy for agents that forget between shifts is written hand-over artefacts each new session reads first.[1]

four-names.title: Four names
four-names.script: That skill has names now. Four of them. Prompt engineering. Context engineering. Harness engineering. Graph engineering.

prompt-and-context.title: Prompt and context
prompt-and-context.script: Prompt engineering is how you phrase the ask, as a clear brief nobody could misread. Context engineering is the background you hand over: the budget, the headcount, the culture, the past events.

harness-and-graph.title: Harness and graph
harness-and-graph.keywords: the tools, the workflow across agents
harness-and-graph.script: Harness engineering is the tools and the environment you give access to: the booking system, the caterer contacts, the calendar. Graph engineering is managing the workflow across several agents. Project management, for AI.

newest-term.title: Newest term
newest-term.script: Graph engineering is the newest of the four. The term has only been around since the middle of this year, and people still argue about exactly what it covers. Treat it as new, and unsettled.
